title: The Roman Empire
text: The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome and one of the most influential civilizations in world history. At its height under Emperor Trajan (117 CE), it encompassed territories from Britain to Mesopotamia, with a population of approximately 50–90 million people. Latin, the empire's official language, formed the basis of the Romance languages (French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Romanian). Roman law, engineering feats (aqueducts, roads, the Colosseum), and administrative systems profoundly shaped Western civilization. The Western Roman Empire officially fell in 476 CE when the Germanic chieftain Odoacer deposed the last emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
